newsitem.title: USA: ValuJet posts $22 million net loss for third quarter.
newsitem.headline: ValuJet posts $22 million net loss for third quarter.

text.p: ValuJet Airlines Inc. Tuesday posted a $22 million net loss for the third quarter, when its entire fleet was grounded for all but one day following a fatal crash of one of its jets in the Florida Everglades in May.

The discount airline, which became a wholly owned subsidiary of ValuJet Inc. in a restructuring last month, said the loss, which equalled 40 cents a share, compared with a profit of $22.7 million, or 38 cents a share, a year ago.

"Although ValuJet flew for only one day during the third quarter, our balance sheet, including $179 million of cash in the bank, continues to be among the strongest in the entire industry," ValuJet Inc. Chairman Robert Priddy said in a brief statement.

ValuJet, which realigned its management this month, resumed flight operations Sept. 30 after being grounded by federal regulators following the May 11 crash in Florida that killed all 110 people aboard its Flight 592 out of Miami.
The company said its third-quarter results included nonrecurring charges of $23 million directly resulting from ValuJet's suspension of operations.

ValuJet, which appointed former TWA and Continental Airlines executive D. Joseph Corr as president and chief executive on Nov. 4, said total revenues for the quarter were a mere $311,000, compared with $109.3 million in the 1995 quarter.
The airline said it had only $17,000 in passenger revenue and no revenue from cargo operations in the quarter.
For the first nine months of the year ValuJet said it posted a net loss of $20.9 million, or 38 cents a share, compared with net income of $48.6 million, or 82 cents a share, last year.
Those results included one-time charges of $54.7 million, ValuJet said.
Revenues for the nine months fell 25 percent to $191.5 million from $257.0 million due to the company's suspension of operations during the third quarter, the company said.
ValuJet's stock lost 6.25 cents to $10.625 in early trading on the Nasdaq market.
